Starting a family is one of life’s most cherished dreams. However, for many couples, conceiving naturally may take longer than expected or require medical support. Thanks to significant advancements in reproductive medicine, In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) has helped millions of couples worldwide experience the joy of parenthood.

If you are searching for the best IVF specialist in Noida, choosing the right fertility expert is one of the most important decisions you will make. IVF treatment is more than a medical procedure—it is a journey that requires expertise, transparency, emotional support, and personalized care.

In this comprehensive guide, we’ll explain everything you need to know about selecting an IVF specialist, understanding fertility treatments, factors that influence success rates, and what to expect during your fertility journey.

Why Choosing the Right IVF Specialist Matters

Every couple’s fertility journey is unique. Factors such as age, medical history, hormonal balance, ovarian reserve, sperm quality, lifestyle, and previous pregnancies all play a role in determining the most suitable treatment approach.

An experienced IVF specialist helps by:

  • Identifying the underlying cause of infertility
  • Recommending the most appropriate treatment
  • Creating an individualized fertility plan
  • Using evidence-based treatment protocols
  • Monitoring each stage of the IVF cycle carefully
  • Providing emotional guidance throughout the process

A patient-focused approach not only improves treatment efficiency but also helps couples make informed decisions with confidence.

Understanding IVF Treatment

IVF, or In Vitro Fertilization, is an advanced fertility treatment in which an egg and sperm are fertilized outside the body in a specialized laboratory. The resulting embryo is then transferred into the uterus with the goal of achieving pregnancy.

IVF may be recommended for couples experiencing:

  • Blocked or damaged fallopian tubes
  • Ovulation disorders
  • Endometriosis
  • Male infertility factors
  • Unexplained infertility
  • Low ovarian reserve
  • Previous unsuccessful fertility treatments
  • Advanced maternal age

Modern IVF techniques continue to evolve, offering improved precision and better treatment outcomes for many patients.

Qualities of the Best IVF Specialist in Noida

Finding the right fertility specialist involves more than checking online reviews. Here are the most important qualities to consider:

1. Specialized Experience

Look for a fertility specialist with extensive experience in reproductive medicine and assisted reproductive technologies. Experience often translates into better clinical judgment, especially in complex fertility cases.

2. Personalized Treatment Plans

No two patients are alike.

The best IVF specialists evaluate:

  • Medical history
  • Hormonal profile
  • Ultrasound findings
  • Ovarian reserve
  • Semen analysis
  • Lifestyle factors

before designing a customized treatment protocol.

Avoid clinics that recommend identical treatment plans for every patient.

3. Comprehensive Fertility Evaluation

Successful IVF begins with accurate diagnosis.

A detailed fertility assessment may include:

For Women

  • Hormonal evaluation
  • AMH testing
  • Ultrasound scan
  • Ovulation assessment
  • Fallopian tube evaluation
  • Thyroid function tests

For Men

  • Semen analysis
  • Hormonal testing (when required)
  • DNA fragmentation testing (in selected cases)
  • Physical examination

Identifying the exact cause of infertility helps optimize treatment decisions.

4. Advanced IVF Technology

Modern fertility centers use advanced laboratory techniques to improve embryo development and treatment precision.

These may include:

  • ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection)
  • Blastocyst culture
  • Time-lapse embryo monitoring
  • Cryopreservation (egg, sperm, embryo freezing)
  • Assisted hatching (when appropriate)
  • Preimplantation genetic testing (in selected cases)

Access to advanced technology can support individualized treatment plans, depending on the patient’s clinical needs.

Signs You Should Consult an IVF Specialist

Many couples wait too long before seeking medical advice.

Consider consulting a fertility specialist if:

  • You are under 35 and have been trying to conceive for over one year.
  • You are over 35 and have been trying for six months.
  • You have irregular menstrual cycles.
  • You have experienced recurrent miscarriages.
  • You have known PCOS or endometriosis.
  • Your partner has abnormal semen analysis.
  • You have undergone previous unsuccessful fertility treatments.
  • You have undergone surgery involving the reproductive organs.

Early consultation often helps identify issues sooner and may expand available treatment options.

Questions to Ask During Your First Fertility Consultation

Being prepared can make your consultation more productive.

Consider asking:

  • What tests will I need?
  • What is the likely cause of infertility?
  • Which treatment is most suitable for us?
  • What are the expected timelines?
  • Are there alternatives to IVF?
  • How many monitoring visits are required?
  • What lifestyle changes do you recommend?
  • What support services are available during treatment?

A good fertility specialist will take the time to answer your questions clearly and honestly.

Common Fertility Treatments Before IVF

IVF is not always the first recommendation.

Depending on your diagnosis, your specialist may suggest:

TreatmentBest For
Ovulation InductionIrregular ovulation
Timed IntercourseMild fertility concerns
IUI (Intrauterine Insemination)Mild male factor infertility or unexplained infertility
Fertility PreservationIndividuals planning future pregnancies
IVFModerate to complex infertility cases
ICSISignificant male factor infertility

Choosing the right treatment depends on a thorough evaluation and individualized medical advice.

Factors That Influence IVF Success

While IVF has helped many couples achieve pregnancy, success depends on several factors, including:

  • Age of the female partner
  • Egg quality
  • Sperm quality
  • Embryo quality
  • Uterine health
  • Lifestyle habits
  • Underlying medical conditions
  • Adherence to treatment protocols

It’s important to understand that no clinic or doctor can ethically guarantee pregnancy, as outcomes vary from person to person.

Why Experience Matters When Choosing an IVF Specialist

IVF is a highly specialized treatment that requires careful planning, precise laboratory processes, and continuous monitoring. An experienced fertility specialist understands that every patient’s fertility challenges are different and creates a treatment plan based on individual medical needs rather than following a standard approach.

A qualified IVF specialist focuses on:

  • Comprehensive fertility evaluation
  • Personalized treatment planning
  • Transparent communication
  • Ethical medical practices
  • Continuous monitoring throughout the IVF cycle
  • Emotional support for couples

Experience also helps in managing complex fertility cases, including repeated IVF failures, low ovarian reserve, endometriosis, PCOS, and male infertility.

Step-by-Step IVF Treatment Process

Understanding the IVF process can help reduce anxiety and prepare couples for the journey ahead.

Step 1: Initial Consultation

The first appointment includes a detailed discussion about:

  • Medical history
  • Previous pregnancies
  • Lifestyle
  • Menstrual history
  • Existing medical conditions
  • Previous fertility treatments

Your specialist may recommend diagnostic tests before designing your treatment plan.

Step 2: Fertility Assessment

Tests may include:

Female Fertility Tests

  • AMH Test
  • Hormonal Profile
  • Ultrasound Scan
  • Thyroid Function
  • Vitamin D Levels

Fertility medications stimulate the ovaries to produce multiple mature eggs instead of the single egg released during a natural menstrual cycle.

During this phase, the specialist monitors follicle growth using:

  • Ultrasound scans
  • Blood hormone tests

Medication doses may be adjusted based on individual response.

Step 4: Egg Retrieval

Once the eggs reach maturity, they are collected through a minimally invasive procedure performed under mild anesthesia.

The procedure usually takes around 20–30 minutes, and most patients return home the same day.

Step 5: Fertilization

The collected eggs are fertilized in a specialized IVF laboratory using either:

  • Conventional IVF
  • ICSI (Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection)

The embryology team carefully monitors embryo development over the following days.

Step 6: Embryo Development

Healthy embryos are cultured for several days before the specialist determines the most suitable time for embryo transfer.

Embryo quality plays an important role in treatment planning.

Step 7: Embryo Transfer

The selected embryo is transferred into the uterus using a thin catheter.

The procedure is generally painless and does not require surgery.

Step 8: Pregnancy Test

Around 10–14 days after embryo transfer, a blood test is performed to determine whether implantation has occurred.

Lifestyle Habits That May Support Fertility

Although medical treatment is essential in many cases, healthy lifestyle habits may support overall reproductive health.

A balanced diet helps maintain overall health during fertility treatment.

Common Myths About IVF

Myth 1: IVF Always Works on the First Attempt

Fact: Success depends on several medical factors, including age, embryo quality, and overall reproductive health. Some couples may require more than one treatment cycle.

Myth 2: IVF Is Only for Women

Fact: Male infertility contributes to many infertility cases. Both partners should undergo evaluation.

Myth 3: IVF Always Results in Twins

Fact: Modern IVF often involves transferring a single embryo when appropriate, reducing the likelihood of multiple pregnancies.

Myth 4: IVF Is Extremely Painful

Fact: Most IVF procedures involve only mild discomfort, and egg retrieval is typically performed under anesthesia.

Myth 5: Age Doesn’t Matter Because IVF Can Solve Everything

Fact: Female age remains one of the most significant factors influencing fertility and IVF outcomes.

Not always. Depending on the diagnosis, your specialist may recommend lifestyle changes, ovulation induction, or intrauterine insemination (IUI) before considering IVF.

A complete IVF cycle generally takes around 4–6 weeks, although the exact duration varies depending on the individual’s treatment protocol and response to medication.

Maintaining a healthy weight, eating a balanced diet, exercising regularly, avoiding smoking and excessive alcohol, and managing stress can support overall reproductive health. However, medical evaluation is important if conception is delayed.

ICSI vs IVF: Overcoming Severe Male Factor Infertility

Male factor infertility accounts for almost half of the cases of infertility and is sometimes wrongly blamed as a health problem in women. There are now highly specific treatments available in modern reproductive medicine that can help address these issues related to the sperm.

Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) can be carried out using two main techniques: traditional IVF and Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI). Both methods are geared towards creating this situation for a healthy pregnancy, but your diagnostic results will determine if you wish to pursue one method compared to the other. At Little Angel IVF, we devote time to examining your individual biological markers and charting a course for the most personalized treatment.

Understanding Traditional IVF

In conventional IVF, the eggs are retrieved and the sperm is then prepared before being combined into a controlled environment for a woman’s laboratory. It is generally advised by a specialist for conditions of the female partner, such as blocked fallopian tubes or irregular periods of menstruation when there are no abnormalities of the male partner’s semen.

The chief merit of its use is that it does not involve any artificial selection, but traditional IVF has a significant disadvantage. Where there are significant functional problems, even though the sperm on paper may look sound, it can lead to complete failure of fertilisation.

What is ICSI?

Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection, or ICSI treatment, is a special form of precision embryology that is used to address very difficult male infertility cases. The basic steps used in ovarian stimulation and egg retrieval are the same as those used in regular IVF in India, but the main difference occurs within the embryology lab.

An embryologist working with a high-magnification microscope and advanced micromanipulation equipment would be able to pick up a single structurally normal live sperm and inject it into the centre of a mature egg with a micro needle. The ICSI procedure circumvents the problem of the sperm having to travel to and perforate the outside membrane of the egg without assistance, and hence the most common physical impediments to fertilisation are avoided.

ICSI vs IVF: Key Differences

FeatureTraditional IVFICSI Treatment
Fertilisation MethodSperm and egg mix naturally in a lab dish.A single sperm is injected directly into the egg.
Suitable PatientsPrimarily female factor or unexplained infertility.Severe male factor infertility or past IVF failures.
Sperm Quality RequiredHigh count, normal motility, and standard shapes.Can work with very low numbers or immotile sperm.
Laboratory PrecisionStandard microscopic observation.High-precision micromanipulation systems.
Fertilisation SuccessDependent on independent sperm performance.Highly predictable fertilisation rates per mature egg.
Cost ConsiderationsStandard pricing structure.Slightly higher due to advanced laboratory tech.
Clinical DecisionChosen when male parameters are optimal.Chosen when sperm requires direct assistance.

When is ICSI Recommended?

When there is serious male infertility involved, an ICSI procedure is usually recommended by a fertility specialist:

  • Low sperm count: Few cells are in a lab dish to guarantee reaching the egg.
  • Poor Sperm Movement: Sperm does not move well enough to reach and attach to the egg.
  • Abnormal Sperm Morphology: Abnormal sperm cannot penetrate the outer layer of the egg.
  • IVF Failure: Strangeness in past traditional IVF attempts causing few or zero fertilised eggs.
  • Surgical Sperm Retrieval: If the sperm is collected directly from the testicles or the epididymis, it tends to be underdeveloped and would need direct injection to fertilise an egg.
  • Frozen Sperm Samples: Cryopreserved sperm may be noticeably low in motility or viability when thawed.

How Precision Embryology Improves ICSI Outcomes

The technical skills of the medical team and the profession that is embryology lab of the treatment center constitute a significant factor in its success. Here, however, the power of precision embryology comes into its own, with the ability to select sperm with the highest genetic integrity.

The team of Dr. Mona Dahiya at Little Angel IVF, utilizes cutting edge micromanipulation tools and digital infrastructure which help to reduce any physical stress on the cells during injection. When used in combination with time-lapse monitoring for unfettered embryo surveillance, this precision assures that only the healthiest embryo is used for transfer, providing optimal odds for pregnancy success.

Does ICSI Increase IVF Success?

Expectations should be practical when a couple is seeking treatment for their relationship issues. In severely infertile men ICSI increases significantly the chances of successful fertilising, but it is not a guarantee to a clinical pregnancy.

These ICSI procedures will provide the sperm with the opportunity of entering the egg and thus stimulating the formation of an embryo. The final success rate of IVF, however, relies on numerous biological factors such as the woman’s age, total strategy quality, embryo quality after fertilization, and receptivity of the uterus. While a top embryology lab has the ability to maximize the early steps, there are always elements of the body to work around to secure a healthy birth as well.

Is Traditional IVF Still a Good Option?

Absolutely. The use of traditional IVF is a very safe and highly effective treatment option for many families. When a thorough fertility assessment concludes that the man’s semen parameters are fully normal, the usual course is to proceed with conventional IVF.

These procedures are selected solely based on factual medical information and not by any random preference of the reproductive specialist. Conventional IVF permits the natural selection process to proceed without additional, invasive clinical handling of the cells, and allows natural fertilisation to safely occur in the laboratory dish.

How Doctors Decide Between ICSI vs IVF

A careful and very individual medical appraisal is needed to work out the best approach. Several important things are reviewed before a definitive clinical recommendation:

  • Complete Semen Exam: complete check-up of number, motility, and morphology of sperm cells.
  • Advanced Sperm Function Tests: When needed, evaluating DNA fragmentation within the sperm.
  • Female Partner Evaluation: Taking into account ovarian reserve, egg quantity, and maternal age.
  • Medical and Treatment History: Finding to see how the cells of the couple react during any past reproductive cycles.

Dr Mona Dahiya states that each couple has its own fertility landscape. All treatment options should be customized to meet the unique diagnostic challenges of each couple to maximize treatment safety and effectiveness toward parenthood.

Why Precision Matters in Modern Fertility Care

In today’s modern reproductive medicine, it is no longer a single-size-fits-all approach. With advanced technology and a wealth of clinical experience, uncertainty surrounding fertility treatment has been greatly diminished for couples.

If you’re struggling with severe male factor infertility, it sometimes depends on the fine details. A controlled process of micromanipulation that is carried out by an experienced embryology team guarantees that each viable egg has the best chance of developing a healthy embryo. These cutting-edge laboratory techniques, coupled with a patient, compassionate approach, give couples clarity, safety, and confidence in their family-building process.

Conclusion

Traditional IVF and ICSI have transformed assisted reproduction and have provided millions of hopeful parents the chance to build a family. While IVF is a great alternative in cases of normal sperm parameters, ICSI is a revolutionary alternative in cases of very low sperm parameters.

With the help of the precision of the procedures of embryology, barriers to fertilisation can now be crossed with great precision. When facing fertility issues, it’s best to find a reputable specialist to understand your choices. At Little Angel IVF, the dedicated medical team led by Dr. Mona Dahiya offers you the care, expertise, and environment to help bring your dream of parenthood to life.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. What is the difference between ICSI vs IVF?

In the traditional IVF process, thousands of sperm are mixed to the egg inside a dish so the egg gets fertilized naturally. In ICSI, an experienced embryologist carefully picks one healthy sperm and carefully places it into an egg with a microscope.

2. Is ICSI better than IVF for male infertility?

Yes. ICSI treatment is exclusively used for Male factor infertility. The first test comes back low sperm count, poor motility, or abnormal shape, ICSI overcomes these problems by allowing the sperm to be placed directly inside the egg.

3. Does ICSI guarantee pregnancy?

No. Most pregnancies produced artificially with ICSI will still be affected by the quality of the eggs, the age of the woman, embryo development and the health of the uterine lining.

4. Who should choose ICSI treatment?

ICSI is best suited for couples where the man has very poor sperm motility, those who have frozen sperm or for couples who have undergone a previous conventional IVF cycle that failed due to problems with their male partner.

5. ICSI vs IVF, which is more expensive in India?

Yes, the cost of ICSI is little more expensive. This involves the high-end micromanipulation technologies, powerful microscopes and advanced embryology skills needed to carry out the procedure.

Intrauterine Insemination (IUI)

Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI)

Preimplantation Genetic Testing (PGT)

Blastocyst Culture

Blastocyst culture allows embryos to develop to the Day-5 stage before transfer. This extended culture period helps embryologists identify embryos with better developmental potential and may improve embryo selection in appropriate cases.

Frozen Embryo Transfer (FET)

Frozen Embryo Transfer enables previously cryopreserved embryos to be transferred in a later menstrual cycle. FET provides flexibility in treatment planning and can be recommended when the uterine environment is more favorable or when embryos have been stored for future pregnancy attempts.

Fertility Preservation

Fertility preservation involves freezing eggs, sperm, or embryos for future use. It is a valuable option for individuals planning delayed parenthood or those undergoing medical treatments that could affect fertility.

Laser Assisted Hatching

Laser Assisted Hatching is an advanced laboratory technique that may help facilitate embryo implantation by assisting the embryo in hatching from its outer shell before transfer. It is recommended only in carefully selected clinical situations.

Hysteroscopy

Hysteroscopy is a minimally invasive procedure that allows direct visualization of the uterine cavity. It helps diagnose and treat conditions such as polyps, adhesions, uterine septum, or fibroids that may interfere with implantation or pregnancy.

Laparoscopy

Laparoscopy is performed to diagnose and manage conditions such as endometriosis, pelvic adhesions, ovarian cysts, or tubal disorders. In selected patients, treating these conditions surgically may improve natural fertility or enhance IVF outcomes.

1. When should I consult an IVF specialist?

3. Does every infertile couple need IVF?

No. Many couples conceive with lifestyle modifications, ovulation induction, or IUI. IVF is recommended only when medically indicated after proper evaluation.

4. What is the difference between IVF and IUI?

IUI places prepared sperm directly inside the uterus to improve the chances of fertilization, while IVF involves fertilizing eggs with sperm in a laboratory before transferring the embryo into the uterus. The appropriate treatment depends on the underlying cause of infertility.

8. What is PGT?

Preimplantation Genetic Testing (PGT) evaluates embryos for certain chromosomal abnormalities before embryo transfer. It may be recommended for selected couples based on age, recurrent miscarriages, or known genetic conditions.

9. Can infertility affect men as well?

Yes. Male factors contribute to nearly half of infertility cases. This is why fertility specialists evaluate both partners before recommending treatment.

10. How long does an IVF cycle take?

PGT-A Testing in India: Is It Needed for Every IVF Cycle?

In recent years, there have been numerous advances in the area of fertility treatments, and one of those advances is genetic screening, referred to as PGT-A testing.

At Little Angel IVF, couples often ask whether they need to have their embryos assessed for chromosomes in order to have a successful IVF treatment. The short answer? No. It can alter lives, save pregnancies, and even be used to identify healthy embryos, but it is an expensive procedure and is not always necessary on every trip. / / Dr. Mona Dahiya feels the best approach is to go above and beyond the traditional norms and only suggest cutting-edge procedures when they are applicable to your medical and financial condition.

What Is PGT-A Testing?

Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Aneuploidies is known as PGT-A. It is used in filtering out embryos created during the IVF process so that the embryos can be transferred to the uterus with the correct number of chromosomes. / / The number of chromosomes needed for a healthy embryo is 46. The most common cause of embryonic failure or early pregnancy loss is defects in the number of chromosomes. Experts can utilize screening to determine and select the embryos that have the right mix of genes and have the highest likelihood of leading to a healthy pregnancy.

How Is PGT-A Performed During IVF?

Eggs are retrieved and placed in the lab for 5 to 6 days of embryo culture to produce a “blastocyst.”

At the time of maturity, an embryologist will take a few cells from the outer layer that creates the placenta in a safe day 5 blastocyst biopsy.

These embryos are safely frozen while the cells are being tested genetically. After a couple of weeks, the genetic testing is completed and a euploid embryo transfer will be carried out, in which a healthy genetically normal embryo is carefully placed into the uterus.

Who Needs PGT-A Testing in IVF?

It is mainly used to help certain groups of patients achieve the best chance of pregnancy. The main groups who benefit include:

  • Women over 35: Age can bring about changes in egg quality, which bring greater risks of abnormalities in the chromosomes.
  • Recurrent IVF failure: Useful if several IVF cycles with good quality embryos have not resulted in pregnancy.
  • Recurrent miscarriage causes: Identifies genetic issues that may cause recurrent miscarriage.
  • Previous genetic conditions: If a previous pregnancy had an abnormality, it might be helpful to include this.

However, it is not essential for most young couples. If the woman is below 35 years of age during her first cycle, then she won’t require further tests because her baseline is already high.

Is Genetic Testing Mandatory for IVF in India?

The simple answer is no. Should there be a genetic test for IVF in India? Not at all. There is no law or doctor’s rule that mandates using genetic screening as part of your standard IVF treatment.

Deciding whether or not to pursue this screening will depend solely on your age, your medical history, the quality of your embryos, and your physician’s recommendations. It is always a joint decision between you and your fertility team.

We don’t like to over-treat patients or impose extra costs on your journey at Little Angel IVF. If there is a favorable general health assessment, then it might be best to have a regular IVF and not do extra genetic screening.

Is PGT Testing Worth It for IVF Under 35?

Young women (mostly under 35) have a high number of unaltered and healthy eggs available naturally. This means that your embryos have a very high probability of having the correct number of chromosomes by themselves. The screening adds a significant financial burden to these common cases, but does not really affect the final success rates.

PGT-A Test Success Rate India

The data on the success of the PGT-A test on Indian couples reveals that when a screened embryo is transferred, the risk of miscarriage is significantly reduced and the pregnancy time is shortened. Using normal embryos eliminates statistically failed cycles and guarantees optimum cycle safety.

However, a successful pregnancy still depends on other critical biological elements:

  • The integrity of cells: The first quality of the original sperm and egg cells.
  • Uterine Receptivity: The health and blood flow of the uterine lining and the thickness of the lining.
  • Systemic Health: Metabolic health, age, and normal hormone levels at the start of the transfer cycle.

PGT-A Testing Cost in India

It is important to have an idea of the financial component when budgeting. The overall price of PGT-A in India normally ranges between ₹25,000 and ₹35,000 per embryo. The cost of base treatment is also likely to go up by ₹1 lakh to ₹1.5 lakh because 4-5 embryos are tested in the lab. / / As it is a state-of-the-art infrastructure, the cost of preimplantation genetic testing in India depends on the city, lab, and case at hand. We strive to be fully transparent about the costs at Little Angel IVF and give you a clear breakdown of the costs that is tailored to your medical requirements.

Are There Any Risks Involved?

Any type of handling outside the body has a small risk, but modern IVF labs have brought this down significantly in the past decade.

A skilled embryologist can carry out the biopsy with utmost safety in only a few seconds in a high-quality lab by utilizing ultra-precise lasers. With the expert management of a team, the real risk of embryo damage is extremely small, typically less than 1 percent.

Conclusion

Overall, PGT-A is an extraordinarily useful tool that holds great promise for certain subgroups of fertility patients. It can expedite a woman’s journey to pregnancy, especially for older women or women who have had multiple miscarriages. But it is not required for all IVF cycles.

Fertility treatments should always be suited to your personal medical history, cost and comfort. Book an appointment with us and select the appropriate path, it takes the assistance of an open, honest fertility expert who is not looking for extra diagnostic tests.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Does a normal PGT-A report guarantee a 100% successful pregnancy?

No. It does tell you that the embryo contains the correct number of chromosomes, but you need to have a healthy uterus, hormone levels and lining receptivity to be successful.

2. Can PGT-A cause long-term birth defects in the baby?

No, just a few cells are removed in the biopsy from the outer layers (placenta). The inner cells which form the baby remain unaffected.

3. How much does the average PGT-A testing cost in India?

The cost of the PGT-A testing in India is typically about ₹25,000 to ₹35,000 per embryo, and ultimately depends on the number of embryos that are being tested.

4. What is PGT-A testing?

PGT-A tests the whole chromosome complement without discriminating against particular ones for random abnormalities such as Down syndrome.

5. Can I choose the gender of my baby using PGT-A testing in India?

No. Gender selection is illegal and is punishable in India by the PCPNDT Act.The test is only taken to pick up medical abnormalities.

Feb 23, 2026Fertility

When you decide to become parents and find out that because of some or other reasons, you are not able to conceive. You decide to consult a doctor and the first thing the doctor will ask is to get some tests done. To figure out the exact problem that is causing infertility, it is important that you get those tests done and based on the results you proceed further. HSG test is one of those, which your doctor might ask you to get done before proceeding the actual treatment.

What is the HSG Test?

HSG stands for Hysterosalpingogram. It is to check your uterus and fallopian tubes for any kind of blockage or structural issues.

Why is the HSG test important?

While there are a lot of issues that can cause infertility. In India, 1 out of 4 women are facing infertility issues because of tubal factor or blocked fallopian tubes. The blocked fallopian tubes will not let the sperm or egg meet and make natural conception almost impossible and extremely difficult. Hence the HSG test plays a vital role in the diagnostic phase of your fertility treatment.

Why would a doctor ask you to get a HSG test done?

  1. When you are trying for the past 1 year and unable to conceive.
  2. When you want to go for IUI treatment
  3. If you have a history of pelvic infections, endometriosis, or a previous ectopic pregnancy.
  4. In case of recurrent miscarriages
  5. If there is any history of abdominal surgeries

How to prepare for the HSG test ?

Ideally, the HST test is scheduled after 7-10 days of your first day of period. The timing is usually before ovulation to make sure that there is no pregnancy. The uterine lining is thin and it is good for clear X-ray images.

Your Doctor might ask you the following questions before the HSG test:

  1. If you have any allergy to iodine or contrast dye?
  2. If there are any chances of pregnancy?
  3. If there is heavy vaginal bleeding?
  4. If there is any kind of pelvic infection?
  5. If there are any symptoms of STI?

Your doctor can recommend you to take a pain reliever like ibuprofen one hour before the test is performed to manage the cramping during or after the HSG test. Also, you should make sure to have a comfortable ride to go back home as there might be some minor cramps pain after the test.

HSG Test Procedure

The HSG test is often done within 5-10 minutes. It is a quick process and doesn’t take long. The entire HSG test process is as mentioned below:

  1. You will have to lie on a table with your knees bent, just like a routine pelvic exam.
  2. Your doctor will insert a speculum to widen the vagina and cleans the cervix with an antiseptic.
  3. A small, thin tube is inserted into the cervix. The speculum is then removed.
  4. The doctor will slowly pump the contrast dye into your uterus. You might feel some period-like cramping her which is absolutely normal.
  5. When the dye flows, the X ray images will be taken. The doctor will ask you to move and shift positions so the movement of dye can be analysed properly.
  6. The catheter will be removed when there are enough clear images for analysis and the test is done.

Is the HSG Test painful?

This is usually the most curious question for most of the women. It might feel like intense menstrual cramping that lasts only for 2- 5 minutes while the dye is being injected. A slight pinch or pressure can also be felt during insertion of the catheter. The pain level is mild to moderate.

HSG Test with Anesthesia – Generally anaesthesia isn’t required as the pain is mild and feels like intense period cramps. However, some clinics offer the test with anaesthesia at an additional cost.

HSG Test Price and Cost

In Delhi NCR, the cost of HSG test is quite affordable as compared to other invasive diagnostic surgeries. Below mentioned is the cost breakdown for HSG test procedure-

Service TypeEstimated Cost (INR)
Standard HSG Test₹2,500 – ₹5,500
HSG test cost with anesthesia₹5,500 – ₹9,500
Premium Clinic / Digital HSG₹8,000+

Factors that impact the cost of HSG test –

  1. Type of dye that is being used : There are various types of dyes, oil based or water based. Oil based dyes are slightly more expensive and preferred because of their potential fertility-boosting flushing effect.
  2. Anesthesia cost : If a patient chooses to take anesthesia for the procedure, it will increase the cost as it involves an anesthesiologist and specialized monitoring.
  3. Imaging Technology: Premium clinics often use digital imaging to ensure the most accurate diagnosis as they provide much clearer images than older analog machines. Digital imaging techniques are relatively costlier than the older ones.
  4. Insurance reimbursements : Some insurance companies include these tests in their policy. You must check with your insurance company to see if you can claim the reimbursement and save money.

While cost is a factor, the HSG test provides you the clarity to take the right treatment. After knowing whether your fallopian tubes are open or blocked, your fertility expert can start a targeted treatment plan that works best for you.

Blocked HSG Test

After analysing the X ray images, if the fallopian tubes are found blocked it is called a blocked HSG test. You don’t have to worry as this doesn’t mean you can’t get pregnant but the blocked HSG test result gives you the clarity around how you should proceed further. Usually the next step is laparoscopy to clear the blocked tubes or your doctor might recommend you to choose IVF as a treatment, which bypasses the tubes entirely.

Benefits of The HSG Test

To start with, the most important benefit that you get from this test is the diagnostic clarity. There are a few more additional benefits which a patient gets after going through the HSG procedure such as:

The flushing effect: When dye is passed through the fallopian tubes, it can clear the minor obstructions like mucus plugs or small debris.

Saving time and resources: After getting the diagnostic clarity of fallopian tubes, doctors can guide you for the best suitable and simpler treatments such as IUI. This saves your money and time both which you might be spending on treatments which are not even possible with blocked tubes.

Uterus Structural health: Along with the fallopian tubes, this test also helps in finding out the uterus structural issues. This ensures there are no polyps or fibroids that might create issues in pregnancy.

Long Term Side effects of HSG Test

There are no long term side effects of the HSG test. Patients usually worry whether the dye or X rays exposure will harm the eggs, fallopian tubes or uterus. But the answer is no, The HSG test is absolutely safe for health. It does not affect your egg quality, menstrual cycles and overall health.

The X rays radiations are also minimal which is equal to the radiations that you might get naturally from the surroundings in a few days. The dye liquid is also safe and it naturally flushes out from the body within a few hours to a day.

While there are no long term effects on your health, you might feel minor discomfort for a few hours. Mild spotting for a day or two, minor pain which feels like menstrual cramps, and dizziness can be felt after the procedure.

Symptoms of pregnancy after HSG test

If the HSG procedure clears out the minor obstructions from the fallopian tubes, there will be more chances of getting pregnant naturally. The symptoms of pregnancy after HSG test are the same as normal pregnancy. Missed periods, tender breasts, mild nausea and fatigue are the most common signs that you can expect. If you are feeling such symptoms, you can confirm it with a pregnancy kit and consult a fertility specialist afterwards to proceed further in your parenthood journey.

FAQs

1. Is the HSG test painful?

It feels like strong period cramps for 5–10 minutes. Most women are back to their daily routine the same day.

2. HSG full form?

It stands for Hysterosalpingogram.

3. When is the best time to do the HSG test?

Ideally between Day 5 and Day 10 of your menstrual cycle.

Jun 11, 2025IVF

For many couples, the journey to parenthood is becoming very challenging due to infertility problems. While 85% of Couples conceive effortlessly, about 15% couples may face difficulties due to various hormonal and lifestyle factors. As a fertility specialist with over 25 years of international experience, I along with my team have helped over 25,000 couples achieve their dream of parenthood both through natural and assisted reproductive interventions.

In this simple and informative blog, I intend to share research backed approaches to boost fertility that applies to both Women and Men. Following these approaches can optimize the chances of conception and help you get pregnant faster—And that too naturally!

UNDERSTANDING FERTILITY: KEY STATISTICS & FACTS

Before I dive into the tips to Boost Fertility naturally, let us look at some fundamental data points that everyone should be aware of.

Peak Fertility Window: A woman is most fertile 5 days before the day of ovulation. Onthe day of ovulation which is usually day 14 of a 28-day cycle.

_(Source: American College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists) _

Age & Fertility Corelation: A healthy 30-year-old woman has a 20% chance of conceiving in every menstrual cycle.This percentage drops to 5% by age the age of 40 Years.

_(Source: Human Reproduction Journal) _

Sperm Health is Not a Myth: About 40-50% of infertility cases these days involve male factors.These are low sperm count and/or Sperm motility. _(Source: WHO) _

Lifestyle Factors Impact: Smoking is now known to reduce fertility by up to 30%.A much worse concern is that obesity can decrease conception chances by up to 50%.

_(Source: Fertility and Sterility Journal) _

7 SCIENTIFICALLY PROVEN WAYS TO ENHANCE FERTILITY NATURALLY.

Enhancing fertility is not a Mystery. Below are 7 Ways to enhance your fertility naturally.

1. Track Your Ovulation Accurately

Timing intercourse around ovulation is crucial to getting pregnant fast. Here is how you can identify your fertile window:

  • Basal Body Temperature (BBT) Tracking:Even a slight rise (0.5°F) in BBT after ovulation indicates fertility. _(Source: Journal of Reproductive Medicine) _
  • Ovulation Predictor Kits (OPKs): Detect the surge in LH levels(24-36) hours before ovulation to plan timing of intercourse.
  • Cervical Mucus Check:An Egg-white-like discharge in Women signals a peak fertility period.

These days there are a lot of Fertility Appslike Flo or Clue that can help predict ovulation with an accuracy of 90% when combined with tracking.

TIP-1: Have intercourse every dayduring the fertile window of the Ovulation period.

2. Optimize Your Diet for Fertility

Nutrition plays a very rolein hormonal balance and overall reproductive health.

Fertility-Boosting Foods:

  • Leafy Greens (Spinach, Kale): Rich in folate, which improves egg quality. (Study: Harvard School of Public Health)
  • Omega-3 Fatty Acids (Flaxseeds, Walnuts, Salmon): Enhances ovulation and sperm motility. (Source: Human Reproduction Update)
  • Antioxidant-Rich Berries: Reduce oxidative stress on eggs and sperm.
  • Whole Grains (Quinoa, Oats): Regulate insulin, which affects ovulation (PCOS women benefit greatly).

Foods to Avoid:

  • Trans Fats (Fast Food, Processed Snacks): Linked to ovulatory infertility. (Study: Nurses’ Health Study II)
  • High-Mercury Fish (Swordfish, Tuna): Can harm foetal development.
  • Excessive Caffeine (>300mg/day): May delay conception. (Source: Fertility and Sterility)

3. Maintain a Healthy Weight

Being underweight or overweightdisrupts hormonal balance.

  • BMI & Fertility: Women with a BMI of 20-24have the highest conception rates.
  • PCOS & Insulin Resistance: Losing 5-10% body weight can restore ovulation in PCOS patients. (Source: Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism)

Exercise Tip: Moderate exercise (yoga, walking) boosts fertility, but excessive workouts (marathon running) may reduce it.

4. Improve Sperm Health

Male fertility contributes to 50% of conception challenges.

Sperm-Boosting Strategies:

  • Take Antioxidants (Vitamin C, E, Zinc): Improves sperm count and motility. (Study: Fertility and Sterility)
  • Avoid Heat Exposure: Tight undergarments, regular hot tubs baths, and laptops on laps reduce sperm quality.
  • Limit Alcohol & Smoking: Heavy drinking lowers the testosterone levels and smoking damages sperm DNA.

Did You Know? It takes about 74 days for any male’ssperms to regenerate. Hence any lifestyle changes take about 2-3 monthsto show the desired effects.

5. Reduce Stress & Boost Sleep

Chronic stress elevates cortisol, disrupting reproductive hormones.

  • Stress & Infertility Link: Women with high stress levels have 29% lower conception rates. (Source: Fertility and Sterility)
  • Relaxation Techniques: Yoga, meditation, and acupuncture improve IVF success rates by 30%. (Study: BMJ)
  • Sleep Matters: Less than 7 hours of sleeplowers fertility hormones like leptin and ghrelin.

My Recommendation: Try mindfulness meditation for 10 mins dailyto lower stress hormones.

6. Avoid Toxins & Environmental Hormone Disruptors

Everyday chemicals can interfere with fertility.

  • BPA (Plastics, Receipts): Mimics estrogen, reducing egg quality. (Source: Environmental Health Perspectives)
  • Pesticides (Non-Organic Produce): Linked to lower sperm count.
  • Parabens (Skincare Products): These Disrupt endocrine function.

Switch To: Glass containers, organic foods, and paraben-free cosmetics.

7. Consider Supplements (After Doctor’s Approval)

Some supplements enhance fertility:

  • Folic Acid (400-800 mcg/day): Prevents neural tube defects and supports ovulation.
  • CoQ10 (100-200 mg/day): Improves egg and sperm quality. (Study: Journal of Assisted Reproduction)
  • Vitamin D: Deficiency is linked to infertility—aim for 30-50 ng/mLlevels.

Caution: Always consult a doctor before starting supplements.

WHEN TO SEE A FERTILITY SPECIALIST?

If you are under 35 and trying for 1 year(or 6 months if over 35) without success, consult a specialist. Common tests include:

  • For Women: Hormonal profiling, ultrasound, HSG (tubal check).
  • For Men: Semen analysis.

Early intervention can prevent delays in conception.

FINAL THOUGHTS

Getting pregnant fast involves a mix of science, timing, and healthy habits. By optimizing ovulation tracking, diet, lifestyle, and stress management, you can significantly boost your chances of conceiving naturally.

As a fertility doctor, my best advice is: Stay patient, stay positive, and trust the process.

What is IVF?

In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) is a revolutionary assisted reproductive technology that has transformed the landscape of infertility treatment. Developed in the late 20th century, IVF involves the process of fertilizing an egg with sperm outside the human body, in a laboratory setting. This technique was primarily designed to help individuals or couples who struggle with infertility to conceive a child. IVF has provided hope to those who face challenges in conceiving due to various medical conditions, such as blocked fallopian tubes, low sperm count, or unexplained infertility.

In this article, we study about IVF decide gender or also about IVF Costs.

What is Gender selection with IVF?

Sex selection, also known as gender selection, is a controversial aspect of IVF that raises ethical, cultural, and social concerns. It refers to the process of choosing the sex of a baby before conception, and it can be achieved through various methods, one of which is IVF.

In the context of IVF, sex selection involves a technique known as preimplantation genetic testing (PGT). This technique allows embryologists to analyze embryos created through IVF for genetic traits or abnormalities before they are implanted into the uterus. PGT involves the removal of a few cells from the embryo and examining their genetic makeup. This analysis provides information about the embryo’s sex, along with any potential genetic disorders.

Can IVF Determine the Gender of a Baby?

Yes, IVF with PGT can determine the gender of a baby before it is implanted in the uterus. By analyzing the genetic information of the embryos, fertility clinics can identify which embryos are male and which are female. This information can then be used to select embryos of a desired sex for implantation. This process is often chosen by parents who have a strong preference for a specific gender, whether due to cultural reasons, family balance, or personal preference.

Can IVF Decide Gender in India?

The practice of gender selection through IVF is a subject of both interest and controversy in India. The Indian government has taken steps to regulate the use of IVF for gender selection due to concerns about gender imbalance and the potential for sex-selective practices that favor male children. Gender-based abortion and discrimination against female children have been issues of significant concern in the country.

The Preconception and Prenatal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act in India prohibits the use of technologies that allow the selection of a specific gender before conception. However, there have been reports of clinics attempting to circumvent these regulations, highlighting the challenges of enforcing such laws effectively.

PGD and PGS/PGT-A Testing Process for Gender Selection:

Preimplantation Genetic Diagnosis (PGD) and Preimplantation Genetic Screening (PGS), also known as Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Aneuploidies (PGT-A), are the key techniques utilized in gender selection during IVF.

  1. PGD: PGD involves the screening of embryos for specific genetic traits, including gender. This technique requires extracting a few cells from the embryos created through IVF. These cells are then genetically analyzed to determine the gender of each embryo. Once the gender is identified, parents can opt to implant embryos of their desired gender into the uterus during the IVF process.
  2. PGS/PGT-A: PGS, now commonly referred to as PGT-A, is a broader technique that primarily aims to identify chromosomal abnormalities in embryos. However, it can also provide information about the gender of the embryos. During PGT-A, cells are extracted from the embryos, and their genetic makeup is scrutinized for any chromosomal imbalances. Alongside detecting potential genetic issues, this technique can also reveal the gender of the embryos.

Gender Selection Process:

  1. Ovarian Stimulation: The IVF process commences with the stimulation of the ovaries to encourage the growth of multiple follicles, each housing an egg.
  2. Egg Retrieval: Once the follicles mature, eggs are retrieved from the ovaries via a minor surgical procedure.
  3. Fertilization: In the laboratory, the retrieved eggs are fertilized with sperm, creating embryos.
  4. Cell Extraction: A few days after fertilization, when the embryos have developed into a multicellular stage, a few cells are carefully extracted from each embryo.
  5. Genetic Analysis: The extracted cells undergo genetic analysis to determine the gender of each embryo. This analysis is performed using specialized techniques that identify the presence of XX chromosomes (female) or XY chromosomes (male).
  6. Embryo Selection: Armed with the gender information, prospective parents can now choose embryos of their preferred gender for implantation.
  7. Implantation: The selected embryos are implanted into the uterus in hopes of achieving a successful pregnancy.

IVF Gender Selection Success Rates with PGS/PGT-A/PGD:

IVF gender selection, enhanced by techniques like Preimplantation Genetic Screening (PGS), Preimplantation Genetic Testing for Aneuploidies (PGT-A), and Preimplantation Genetic Diagnosis (PGD), offers hope to parents aiming to choose the gender of their future child. While success rates can vary, these advanced techniques have elevated the precision and accuracy of gender selection during the IVF process.

PGS/PGT-A and PGD increase the likelihood of selecting embryos of the desired gender. PGS/PGT-A is particularly adept at identifying chromosomal abnormalities, which in turn, enhances the overall success of IVF by facilitating the selection of healthy embryos. PGD, on the other hand, hones in on specific genetic traits, including gender, further refining the selection process.

Success rates are influenced by factors such as the age of the prospective mother, the quality of the embryos, and the expertise of the medical team. Typically, success rates for IVF gender selection can range from 60% to 80%, providing promising prospects for those pursuing this option.

Cost of IVF for Gender Selection:

The cost of IVF for gender selection is a multifaceted consideration that encompasses several components. IVF costs can vary significantly based on geographic location, the reputation of the fertility clinic, the complexity of the procedure, and additional services provided. Gender selection adds another layer of complexity, potentially impacting the overall cost.

On average, a standard IVF cycle in the United States can range from $12,000 to $15,000. However, when gender selection techniques such as PGS/PGT-A or PGD are employed, the cost can escalate. These advanced genetic procedures can add around $3,000 to $6,000 to the overall price tag.

It’s essential to account for potential additional costs such as medication, consultations, and possible multiple IVF cycles. As the cost can be substantial, individuals and couples exploring gender selection within IVF should carefully assess their financial readiness and explore insurance coverage options.

Risk of IVF for Gender Selection:

As with any medical procedure, IVF, including gender selection techniques, comes with potential risks and considerations. While the overall safety profile of IVF is favorable, it’s important to be aware of potential challenges.

  1. Multiple Pregnancies: IVF can sometimes result in multiple pregnancies, increasing the risk of complications for both the mother and the babies.
  2. Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome (OHSS): Ovarian stimulation during IVF can lead to OHSS, causing abdominal discomfort and fluid retention.
  3. Failed Implantation: Even with gender selection techniques, not all embryos will successfully implant, potentially leading to failed cycles.
  4. Ethical and Emotional Challenges: The ethical implications of gender selection can lead to emotional and psychological dilemmas, especially if the selected embryos fail to result in a successful pregnancy.
  5. Financial Investment: IVF entails a significant financial investment, which might lead to stress and disappointment if the desired outcomes are not achieved.

Ethical and Social Considerations:

The practice of gender selection within IVF raises important ethical and social considerations. On one hand, it can be argued that parents have the right to make choices about their family planning, including the gender of their child. However, critics argue that gender selection could contribute to reinforcing harmful gender stereotypes, creating a preference for one gender over the other, and perpetuating gender imbalances.

The ethical concerns also extend to the potential consequences of widespread gender selection, such as a skewed gender ratio in societies, which could lead to long-term social and demographic challenges.

Sperm CollectionA fresh sample of Semen is provided by the Husband on the day of egg retrieval. Certain methods like TESE (Testicular Sperm Extraction) or Fine Needle Aspiration (FNA) may be used if the Husband is unable to give naturally.
FertilizationEggs are fertilized Naturally in the Lab or through ICSI (injecting a single sperm into an egg) in cases of Male Infertility. The embryos are monitored for 24 Hours for development. These are then Cultured for (3-5) Days for Embryo selection.
Embryo TransferHealthiest embryos after (3-5) Days of Fertilization are transferred into the uterus using a thin catheter. This procedure requires (10-15) Minutes and does not require Anaesthesia. A Blood test is done (10-14) Days after Transfer to Check Pregnancy.

TYPES OF IVF PROTOCOLS OFFERED AT LITTLE ANGEL IVF

IVF PROTOCOLSWHAT IS IT?WHEN IS IT USED?
Standard IVF ProtocolGiving Medications to Suppress the Natural Ovulation Cycle. This is done by Stimulating the Ovaries with Fertility Hormone Injections/Medicines.The standard IVF protocol is usually used for women with a good ovarian reserve who are under 40 years of age with an egg count of 10-15.
Natural Cycle IVFNo use of Fertility Medications to Stimulate the Ovaries. In this protocol, a Woman’s Natural Cycle is Leveraged. It is best suited for Women under 35 Years with Good AFC & Normal Levels of AMH.Suggested for women at risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). OHSS is defined as follicles count greater than 20with estradiol levels above 3500 pg/mL.
Short IVF ProtocolThe short IVF protocol is about ovarian stimulation using gonadotropins at the beginning of a menstrual cycle. This involves fewer days of medication compared to Standard IVF protocol.It is used for older Age women (Above the Age of 35) or those with low ovarian reserve i.e. Antral Follicle Count less than 10.
Flare IVF ProtocolFlare IVF Protocol Utilizes a “flare” of natural Hormones along with GnRH agonists at the start of the Cycle to boost FSH & LH levels by approximately 50%.The Flare Protocol is used for women with diminished ovarian reserve i.e. (AMH) level below 1.0 ng/mL and an antral follicle count (AFC) of fewer than 5-7 follicles. Also done for poor responders in previous IVF cycles.
Mini IVF/Mild StimulationMini IVF uses a combination of Oral Medication and Injections to induce Ovulation and produce about (3-7) Eggs. It is a Low-Cost IVF Solution with Less Side Effects like Bloating.Mini IVF is suggested for women with a moderate ovarian reserve (AMH 1-3 ng/mL, AFC 5-10, FSH < 10 mIU/mL) who are under 35 years. It is done to minimize costs and medication use and ideal for those sensitive to high doses.
ICSI IVF ProtocolIntracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is a special IVF protocol used for severe male-factor infertility. In this procedure 1 single Healthy (Normal DNA) sperm is injected into a mature egg to enhance fertilization success.ICSI IVF is used for severe male infertility defined as low sperm count under 15 million/mL, poor motility below 40%, or genetic disorders affecting sperm quality.
PGD IVF ProtocolAn IVF procedure using Genetic Testing of Embryos. Embryos (6–8 Cell Stage by Day 3) are biopsied for genetic evaluation using PCR & FISH to identify Disorders and Chromosomal Abnormalities.PGD IVF Protocol is used to screen embryos for genetic disorders before implantation, ensuring healthy pregnancies.
FET ProtocolFET (frozen embryos Transfer) protocol uses Cryopreserved Embryos that are thawed and transferred in a Fresh IVF Cycle.FET Protocol is recommended when fresh transfer is not possible or to optimize for Couples seeking Family planning or preserving fertility for a Later stage.
Blastocyst TransferThis protocol involves transferring embryos to the uterus at the blastocyst stage (i.e. Embryos Grown for 5-6 Days).Blastocyst Transfer is suggested for better embryo selection, higher implantation rates and/or previous failed IVF attempts.
Donor Gametes ProtocolDonor Gametes Protocol involves using eggs or sperm from a donor, recommended for genetic disorders or infertility.Donor Gametes Protocol is suggested for genetic issues, advanced maternal age, or absent/poor-quality gametes.

Understanding Fertility Treatments

In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)

IVF is one of the most common and effective forms of assisted reproductive technology (ART). It involves retrieving eggs from the ovaries and fertilizing them with sperm in a lab. The resulting embryos are then transferred to the uterus.

Intrauterine Insemination (IUI)

IUI is a simpler procedure where washed and concentrated sperm are directly placed into the uterus around the time of ovulation. This increases the chances of fertilization.

Ovulation Induction

Ovulation induction involves using medications to stimulate the ovaries to produce multiple eggs. This can be beneficial for women who have irregular ovulation or are undergoing other fertility treatments.

Egg Freezing and Fertility Preservation

Egg freezing allows women to preserve their eggs for future use. This can be particularly important for those who wish to delay pregnancy or are undergoing medical treatments that may affect their fertility.

Genetic Testing

Genetic testing can identify potential genetic disorders in embryos before implantation. This helps in selecting the healthiest embryos for transfer, increasing the chances of a successful pregnancy.

May 8, 2024Uterine Polyps

Uterine polyps, also known as endometrial polyps, are growths attached to the inner wall of the uterus that extend into the uterine cavity. Arising from the lining of the uterus, these polyps are usually benign (non-cancerous) but can have a significant impact on a woman’s reproductive health and quality of life. In this comprehensive guide, we’ll explore what uterine polyps are, who is affected by them, their symptoms, causes, diagnosis, and the available treatment options.

What are Uterine Polyps?

Uterine polyps are growths that form from the endometrium, the tissue lining the uterus. They vary in size, ranging from a few millimeters — no larger than a sesame seed — to several centimeters, or the size of a golf ball. While they are usually benign, some polyps can be precancerous or cancerous.

Who is Affected by Uterine Polyps?

Uterine polyps are most common in women who are undergoing or have completed menopause, but they can occur at any age during a woman’s reproductive years. Several factors increase the risk of developing uterine polyps, including:

  • Age, particularly women who are 40 to 50 years old.
  • Obesity.
  • High blood pressure.
  • Taking tamoxifen, a drug therapy for breast cancer.
  • Hormonal factors, particularly fluctuations in estrogen levels.
  • Symptoms of Endometrial/Uterine Polyps
  • Many women with uterine polyps do not experience any symptoms. However, when symptoms are present, they may include:
  • Irregular menstrual bleeding such as having frequent, unpredictable periods of variable lengths and heaviness.
  • Bleeding between menstrual periods.
  • Excessively heavy menstrual periods.
  • Vaginal bleeding after menopause.
  • Infertility, which can be the result of polyps blocking the fallopian tubes or interfering with embryo implantation.

What Are Uterine Polyps Cancer Symptoms?

While most uterine polyps are benign, some can become cancerous. Symptoms that might suggest a cancerous transformation include:

Postmenopausal bleeding, which is any bleeding that occurs after menopause.

Persistent, abnormal uterine bleeding if premenopausal.

It is essential to consult a healthcare provider if any of these symptoms occur, as early detection and treatment are crucial for the best outcomes.

Causes of Endometrial/Uterine Polyps

The exact cause of uterine polyps is unknown, but they are associated with hormone levels, particularly estrogen, which seems to promote their growth. Other potential factors include:

  • Chronic inflammation of the uterus.
  • Genetic mutations, which might contribute to the development of polyps.
  • Diagnosis of Endometrial/Uterine Polyps
  • Diagnosing uterine polyps typically involves:
  • Pelvic examination.
  • Transvaginal ultrasound, where a device is used to create images of the uterus.
  • Hysterosonography, which enhances ultrasound images using fluid injected into the uterus.
  • Hysteroscopy, where a thin, flexible telescope is inserted into the uterus for a direct look at the uterine cavity.
  • Endometrial biopsy, involving tissue sample collection from the uterus for lab analysis.
  • Management and Treatment

Treatment for uterine polyps depends on their size, number, whether they cause symptoms, and whether they are suspected or confirmed to be malignant. Options include:

Watchful waiting, especially if the polyps cause no symptoms and are small.

Medication, which can help reduce symptoms but does not eliminate polyps.

Surgical removal, which is often recommended if polyps cause symptoms, are suspected of being cancerous, or if there are infertility issues.

Surgical methods may include hysteroscopic polypectomy, where polyps are removed during a hysteroscopy.

Should I Worry About Uterine Polyps?

While uterine polyps are usually benign, their potential to affect fertility and very rarely, to become cancerous, makes it important to address them. Regular check-ups and discussions with a healthcare provider are essential, particularly if symptoms develop.

Uterine polyps are a common health concern that can affect a woman’s quality of life and fertility. Understanding these polyps, recognizing the symptoms, and undergoing timely diagnosis and management can help mitigate the impact of uterine polyps on a woman’s health. If you suspect you have symptoms of uterine polyps, consult your healthcare provider for a thorough evaluation and appropriate management.
